transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Avery Brooks (Polaris Head of AI), Samir Patel (Polaris Platform Eng), Lena Torres (Polaris Finance), Noah Reed (Polaris CTO)

Summary: quick console tour focused on usage analytics and cost per route, diffs between hosted vs dedicated costs, and export options for finance.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 30–45 minute walkthrough of the Console usage analytics and then leave time for questions, uh Maya will demo the per-route dashboards and cost breakdown, and I'll cover commercial + next steps
00:22 Maya: cool yeah, ok starting share screen, can you see my screen?
00:26 Avery: yep, all good
00:30 Maya: great — so this is the Redwood Console home, first thing we look at is the usage timeline, it's token-level by default, we show generated vs input tokens, you can change the aggregation to hourly/daily, and we automatically attribute to routes (api keys / routes)
00:55 Samir: when you say routes, is that per microservice or per API key? we largely route by team, but we also have a bunch of legacy keys
01:05 Maya: good question — routes are flexible, you can map to API key, route name, or custom tag — most customers set routes to match product features so finance can see cost by feature.
01:20 Noah: curious how accurate the cost numbers are — is it purely token × price or do you include infra overhead like batching effects?
01:35 Ravi: short answer: the Console shows unit token cost using our billing profiles (model variant, quantization, reserved vs on-demand). We also surface an adjusted cost which applies workload-aware multipliers to approximate batching savings and GPU amortization. it's an estimate but it's close enough for budget planning
01:58 Lena: ok, finance cares about predictability — can we get a per-route monthly forecast?
02:10 Maya: yes we have forecast panel under usage analytics, it extrapolates based on historical ingestion and you can pick confidence bands, plus you can run what-if scenarios if you switch to dedicated capacity or enable prefix caching
02:34 Avery: show the per-route dashboard please
02:40 Maya: opening route detail — here you get a route timeline, distribution of sequence lengths, top prompts, error rates, p50/p95 latency and a cost breakdown. note the cost breakdown splits token cost, infra cost (if on dedicated), and add-on charges like persistent KV or storage.
03:10 Maya: i'll click into the "CheckoutFlow" route as an example — you can see last 30 days, tokens by role (input vs output), average sequence length 180 tokens, batch factor, and our estimated cost per 1k requests
03:30 Samir: is that number precise enough to bill internal teams? we don't need dollar-precision but we need an apples-to-apples baseline
03:45 Jordan: many customers use the per-route cost for internal chargebacks; for external billing they'd sync with the raw billing export but the Console is great for trend and anomalies
03:58 Maya: also note you can export per-route usage to BigQuery or CSV, we have a connector; export includes raw tokens, model id, variant, and tags so finance can do custom allocation
04:20 Lena: export to BigQuery — does that include our internal cost rates or just Redwood's unit costs?
04:30 Ravi: export is raw usage + Redwood unit price; you can import into your finance model to apply your rates (e.g., include infra overhead, margin, etc). For Dedicated customers we also include reserved capacity metrics so you can compute amortized GPU cost
04:52 Avery: what about anomalies and cost spikes — can we alert?
05:00 Maya: yes there are alerting rules: token volume thresholds, per-route cost thresholds, latency spikes; alerts can go to Slack, pager or webhook; we also surface top-prompts causing high token usage so you can optimize prompts
05:20 Samir: on the subject of prompts, can we see which prompts led to long sequences? like top-k prompt histogram?
05:30 Maya: yep — prompt sampling is available, we sample requests and show snippets, we also redact PII by default in the UI for hosted flows; for Private we can honor your DLP settings
05:45 Noah: security wise we need to know about SSO and KMS — Lena will want to see SOC2 and encryption at rest details
05:53 Jordan: understood — we'll send the SOC2 summary and KMS integration guide. for SSO we support SAML/Okta + SCIM for user sync and RBAC at the route level.
06:06 Lena: and audit logs — are those granular enough for our compliance team?
06:12 Ravi: audit logs include token-level request ids, user, route, action, and model variant; logs are retained per your contract and can be exported to your SIEM or S3. note: for Private deployments logs stay in your VPC
06:28 Avery: back to cost modelling — can we simulate switching a heavy route to a quantized variant and see estimated savings?
06:35 Maya: yes that's in the Optimize panel — you can run model-mix scenarios and quantization suggestions; for example we recommend q4_0 for non-generation embedding use cases, and you can preview estimated savings per-route and expected quality delta measured via eval sets if you upload them
06:56 Samir: do you support running evals against our holdout prompts? we'd want to measure hallucination rate changes
07:04 Maya: absolutely — you can upload prompt sets and expected outputs, our quality monitoring will run them and show regressions; it's part of Redwood Optimize. We'll include the eval template in the follow-up docs
07:18 Jordan: a quick note on hosted vs dedicated — hosted is easiest but bursty traffic can be cheaper on dedicated if you commit GPU hours; the Console shows a "cost to dedicated" estimator per route
07:33 Lena: what's the typical break-even? like how many tokens per month before dedicated makes sense?
07:40 Jordan: depends on model and SLA, but typically high-volume routes with steady throughput (multi-million tokens/month) see benefits; we'll run Polaris numbers once you send traffic profile
07:52 Avery: show me the per-token breakdown — I want to see where the dollars are going
07:58 Maya: clicking cost stack — here is tokens × model price, infra (amortized), caching savings, and any third-party add-on. you can hover to see formula, and filter by model family (e.g., Llama2-13B opt vs gpt-like)
08:28 Samir: you mentioned prefix/KV caching — if we enable KV cache for session memory, how does that change cost?
08:37 Maya: enabling KV caching reduces repeated prompt tokens by storing context server-side, so downstream token generation drops — Console will estimate savings based on hit rates; we show measured hit rate after enabling so you can tune TTLs
08:56 Noah: on private deployment — latency targets are critical for us, can we see per-route latency SLO charts?
09:05 Maya: yep, per-route latency P50/P95 with trace drilldown; we also show tail latency contributors like model warmup or network. For private we'll include service-level metrics and you'll be able to tune batching windows in the runtime
09:23 Avery: any limits on dashboard retention? we'd like 12 months of daily aggregates
09:28 Ravi: default retention is 90 days raw, 13 months rolled-up; longer retention is available as an add-on, and exports to your storage are recommended for long-term compliance
09:44 Lena: ok finance would like an export template and an example calculation for internal chargebacks
09:50 Jordan: we'll share a sample sheet mapping per-route usage to internal cost centers and show how to integrate the BigQuery export
10:03 Maya: quick detour — here's the anomaly explorer, it surfaces sudden jumps in token cost and the UI suggests top contributing routes and prompts, you can pivot to the raw requests or create an incident ticket
10:26 Samir: how do we handle mixed routing when the same key is used by multiple services?
10:32 Maya: best practice is to migrate to route tags; Console supports retroactive tagging via logs import or runtime header. we can work with your platform team on a rollout plan
10:46 Avery: ok show the billing reconciliation view please
10:49 Maya: billing reconciliation pulls the raw billing export and aligns it with console tags and route mappings, discrepancies are highlighted. for enterprise accounts we provide an end-of-month reconciliation pack
11:05 Lena: any mention about GPU details in the cost report? like GPU type and amortized hours
11:10 Ravi: yes for Dedicated the export includes GPU instance type, utilization, and amortized cost; you can break out per-route GPU hours if you pin routes to capacity pools
11:28 Noah: resilience, what happens if a model variant is OOM or fails, does Console show fallback events?
11:34 Maya: yes, fallbacks and model switches are logged and surfaced; we have automatic fallback policies and you can configure alerts when fallback rate crosses threshold
11:48 Samir: what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot? we want to do a 4-week pilot with sample traffic
11:56 Jordan: typical pilot is 4 weeks: week 0 onboarding & traffic sync, week 1 baseline benchmarking, week 2 apply Optimize suggestions, week 3 measure delta and wrap up with a cost/quality report
12:12 Avery: ok that aligns, we'll try to get sample logs by next week
12:18 Jordan: great — recap of next steps: I'll send pricing + SOC2, Maya will send dashboards and export examples, Samir will provide traffic logs. Anything else?
12:30 Lena: can you also include estimated cost to move CheckoutFlow to dedicated vs hosted?
12:36 Jordan: noted, we'll include dedicated cost estimate in the pricing pack
12:42 Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and schedule the pilot kickoff once logs land
12:47 End of meeting

Notes on transcript: minor transcription errors present (product names like "Redwood Optimize" sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Opti", KV cache sometimes shown as KV cash). Speaker overlaps and fillers kept to maintain authenticity.
